title: Compact regression scrapbook - Rohit Menon
content:
Quick context:
- Running lightweight regression spot-checks on hosted-api text-generation models (v1.3.0 -> v1.4.1 rollout).
- Focused on customer-facing chat completions and a couple of vertical prompts (finance-summary, legal-qa).
- Goal: surface obvious semantic regressions and large style shifts before canary reaches 100%.

Notes-to-self (how I run this):
- Pull 200 random samples from production logs (last 7d), stratified by route: chat (60%), completion (30%), embeddings triggers (10%).
- For each sample, generate output using old model and new model with identical prompts + temperature/pen settings.
- Quick manual pass for high-level regressions, then 40-sample deeper annotation for metrics.
- Save failing examples to "regression-stash-<date>.jsonl" and link to JIRA if reproduces customer-facing break.

Ad-hoc scoring rubric (0-3) - compact for fast passes:
- 0: Clear functional regression: wrong answer/contradiction/hallucination introduced
- 1: Degradation in helpfulness/length/clarity (style drift but still acceptable)
- 2: Equivalent behaviour (minor differences, same conclusions)
- 3: Improvement (shorter, clearer, less hallucination)

Note: for canary decisions, weigh any 0 as blocker for that route unless mitigated by fallback. Multiple 1s -> flag and monitor.

Selected example snapshots (copied raw, redact customer ids) - examples that stood out:
1) Prompt: "Summarize the attached earnings call transcript - highlight risks"
   Old: "Key risks: rising opex, soft guidance, FX headwinds. Management emphasized margin expansion via cost initiatives."
   New: "Key risks: revenue decline from product X, management expects to pivot to services which will increase margins."
   Quick read: introduced a new false claim around pivot to services (not in transcript). Score: 0.
   Hypothesis: new decoding heuristics + temperature tweak allowed spurious extrapolation on sparse signal.

2) Prompt: "Is this contract clause enforceable in CA?" (legal-qa)
   Old: "Likely unenforceable because clause conflicts with California Labor Code 2750. Consider revising."
   New: "Enforceable, with caveats: depends on court interpretation and contract specifics."
   Quick read: flip in polarity -> potential legal risk. Score: 0.
   Action: isolate example, add to regression-suite, escalate to legal-eval queue.

3) Prompt: "Write a 3-bullet product update about new model improvements"
   Old: shorter bullets, explicit quant numbers: "+14% latency reduction"
   New: longer, hedged language: "notable latency improvements expected"
   Quick read: style regression (less precise), Score: 1.

4) Prompt: "Translate: 'La empresa reportó resultados mixtos'"
   Old: "The company reported mixed results."
   New: "The firm reported mixed results, signaling potential instability in orders."
   Quick read: added interpretation not present in source, Score: 1 (lean 0 if customer-facing translation).

Annotation observations (pattern-level):
- Hallucination spikes correlate with requests that have sparse context + presence of numeric tokens in prompt.
- New model seems more "confident" when lacking evidence -> more polarity flips.
- System prompt layering: confirmed we accidentally shipped a slightly different assistant system string on the canary infra (note from infra team). Possible root cause.

Lightweight aggregate (40-sample deep set):
- 0 (blockers): 6/40
- 1 (degrade): 11/40
- 2 (equiv): 20/40
- 3 (improve): 3/40
Notes: blocker ratio 15% -> high for chat route. Recommend holding canary on chat at 10% until mitigations applied.

Hypotheses to test (quick A/B):
- Revert system prompt string to previous version, re-run spot checks on same 40-sample set. If blockers drop by >50% -> root cause likely prompt layering.
- Lower default temperature for chat route from 0.8 -> 0.6 and test.
- Toggle decoding top-k/top-p mix (we changed top-k from 50 -> 40 in v1.4.1) to see effect.

Immediate actions (TODOs):
- [ ] Dump failing examples to reg-suite and attach to JIRA-4852 (assigned to @claire).
- [ ] Run the system-prompt revert on staging and mark results by EOD tomorrow. (owner: me)
- [ ] Add two legal/finance prompts to canary holdout set (so future rollouts check polarity flips specifically).
- [ ] Add metric for "polarity flip rate" in Redwood Console per-route (PM spike idea).

Longer-term ideas (brainstorm):
- Create lightweight automated polarity-checker for binary-answer routes (legal-qa, compliance-checks) using entailment scoring against prompt context.
- Add a tiny 'sanity filter' step that looks for added claims with low context support (counts numerical additions, dates, new named-entities).
- Cross-check any model-change that alters system prompt text as part of deployment CI (blocker flag).

Open questions / notes for follow-up:
- Is the infra/system-prompt change intentional? Slack thread: #infra-rollouts Jan 23. Need to confirm by ops.
- Should we classify 'translations with interpretation' as 0 or 1? My leaning: translations must be literal -> treat as 0 if new meaning added.
- How aggressive do we gate canary on routes with >10% blockers? Existing policy is fuzzy. Propose PR to add explicit thresholds.

Scratch log (short):
- 2026-01-12: pulled 200 samples, did quick triage.
- 2026-01-13: deeper 40-sample annot. 6 blockers -> logged JIRA-4852.
- 2026-01-14: infra confirmed system prompt diff, staging revert queued.
- 2026-01-16: ran temp/top-k ablation, partial improvement but not full.

References / links:
- JIRA-4852 (regression bundle)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serve/pull/1123 (decoding change)
- Slack: #infra-rollouts thread (Jan 23)

Final quick recommendation: pause full canary for chat route (keep at 10%) until system-prompt revert + temperature ablation verified. If revert resolves >50% of blockers, proceed with staged ramp. Otherwise, open an ops + model rollback plan and extend manual review set to 200 examples for next sweep.

-- Rohit

Tags-to-add-on-save: regression, canary-hold, legal-risk, translation, system-prompt
